title: Appendix D core: memoised child tables, group-by-group mode sum, leaves over chunk variables, end-to-end count
spec:
Implement the Appendix D core in appd_core.py. Write the bodies of NodeExpansion.group_table, NodeExpansion.sum_paper, NodeExpansion.sum_memo, NodeExpansion.sum_dp and of the module functions byvars_value, node_value and count_e2e; their docstrings are the contracts and NOTES.md gives the background. Then set IMPLEMENTED = True in appd_core.py and USE_CODE_FLAGS = True in appd_params.py (change nothing else in appd_params.py).

Hints:
1. group_table(g): gammas = self.tuples(self.inc[g], self.p); return {self.key(gm): self.child_network_value(g, gm) for gm in gammas} and add len(gammas) to self.child_calls.
2. sum_paper: tables = {g: self.group_table(g) for g in self.r_groups}; total = [0] * self.q; for beta in self.tuples(list(range(len(self.modes))), self.p): val = [1] + [0] * (self.q - 1); for g in self.r_groups: sub = {k: e for k, e in beta.items() if k in self.inc[g]}; val = ps_mul_mod(val, tables[g][self.key(sub)], self.q, self.m); then total = ps_add_mod(total, val, self.m). Return (total, number of beta, number of beta * len(self.r_groups)).
3. sum_memo: set self.child_calls = 0, then the same sum; return (total, number of beta, self.child_calls).
4. sum_dp: set self.child_calls = 0; tables as above; pos = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(self.r_groups)}; for mode k the ends are self.modes[k]["src"] and self.modes[k]["tgt"]. Phi = {(): [1] + [0] * (self.q - 1)}. At step i with group g: new = the modes k in self.inc[g] whose smaller end position is i and whose larger end position is > i; for every key s in Phi and every nt in self.tuples(new, self.p) with self.weight(dict(s)) + self.weight(nt) < self.p: count it, full = dict(s) with nt added, gamma = full restricted to self.inc[g], val = ps_mul_mod(Phi[s], tables[g][self.key(gamma)], self.q, self.m), proj = full restricted to the modes whose larger end position is > i, and add val into newPhi[self.key(proj)]. max_enum = the largest count of one step. The result is Phi.get((), [0] * self.q) after the last group.
5. byvars_value: follow its docstring. Vertices k with ne.grp[k] == g are the chunks of the group; their variables are the union of net.units[k]; their clauses are the ci with net.desig[ci] among those k; the column bit of a wire w with ne.colg[w] == g is the value of variable _WIREMAP[(id(net), w)][1]; the wire between clause ci and an outside variable v is _WIREMAP[(id(net), "cv", ci, v)]. For each assignment of the variables and each choice of clause terms, compute every packet like packet_tensor does, but with the row factor w0 + (w1 - w0) * form instead of l_Y(form): the local part becomes w0 + (w1 - w0) * loc and each mode coefficient c becomes (w1 - w0) * c. Multiply the packets and the coefficient (+1 or -1) of the chosen terms and add everything up (mod 2^p).
6. node_value: ne = NodeExpansion(net, pk, labels, t, p, q, weights=weights); call the chosen sum; stats as in the docstring.
7. count_e2e: follow its docstring; smoke_appd.py compares it with count_sat.
Pitfalls: series are lists of q ints mod 2^p (self.m); copy dicts before changing them; tuples are dicts {mode: exponent > 0} and self.key(...) is their sorted item tuple; do not call direct_taylor_mod or F_poly inside your functions (the referee blocks them).
stop: smoke_appd.py prints SMOKE OK with IMPLEMENTED = True and USE_CODE_FLAGS = True and every core check line says ok

title: Appendix D parameter search: delta, chunk size, three levels, free u per level
spec:
IMPORTANT: the first attempt explored for the whole 55 minutes and never edited appd_params.py, so it scored nothing. This time, put your first improvement into choose_params within your first 10 steps, run smoke_appd.py, and only then search for more.
Known good starting point (from the earlier attempt's own scans): two levels, r = (7, r1) with r1 between 10 and 21, delta = 0.0002, Lc = 262144 to 1048576 give e of about 0.3300 at lam = 5404 (current 0.33317). The binding term is the root's mode sum, so r0 = 7 is the sweet spot; u_0 is capped by the padding constraint.

Improve the parameter search in appd_params.py (only that file) so that the break-even against 2^(n/3) moves lower. The frozen cost model appd_assembly_public.py (read it, do not edit it) accepts levels 1 to 3, integers r_d in [2, 4096], integers u_d >= 2 and a_d > u_d, delta in [1e-4, 0.25] and Lc in [1, 2^20]; it returns valid = False with a reason when a constraint fails. Ideas: tune delta (for example 0.002 to 0.03) and Lc (256 to 65536); allow three levels; choose u_1 and u_2 freely instead of only rho * u_0; widen the grids of r. Keep the bisection on u_0 for each shape and keep min_a for a_d. choose_params must stay deterministic and under 1 s per call (smoke_appd.py prints the time). Keep USE_CODE_FLAGS = True. Do not touch appd_core.py.

So P1 = log2(r(r+1)/2) (not +1). I used P1 = 1+log2(...) which included the a term. Fine.  Let me now run the big scan. title: Newton (binomial) mode basis and the newton code flag
spec:
Add a second mode basis, the Newton (binomial) basis, to appd_core.py. NOTES.md, section 'Round 6', has the math. Everything that exists must keep working exactly as now: basis='power' is the default everywhere.

1. NodeExpansion.__init__(self, net, pk, labels, t, p, q, weights='paper', basis='power'): accept basis 'power' or 'newton' and store it as self.basis. With basis='newton', inside the existing loop over b:
   - weight: add v2(b!) to the current weight formula, where v2(b!) = b - bin(b).count('1'); stop at the first b whose weight is >= p, as now;
   - source form: lin = [(math.comb(j, b), w2) for j, w2 in cols] without zero coefficients; a mode whose form is empty is not created, but keep the coefficient chain going for the next b;
   - coefficients of row x, with A = Fr(t - y0 + x) and c = step = 2^(i+1): N_0 = the current first series (taylor_at of pk.Wpoly(y0 - x)); N_b = ser_mul(N_(b-1), r_b, q) where r_b is the series of c*b / (A - c*b + alpha z), i.e. Fr(c*b) times ser_inv([A - c*b, alpha] padded or cut to q terms, q). Keep the assertion that every coefficient of N_b has v2 >= the weight, and store [red(x, p) ...] in self.coef[(row wire, mode index)] as now;
   - the (D.12) self-check at the end of __init__ must evaluate the source form with math.comb(j, b) for this basis (j ** b for the power basis). A helper method self.bfun(j, b) is a clean way to do both.
   Keep the data layout: self.modes is a list of dict(P, y0, b, src, tgt, w, lin) in the same order as now (packets, then y0, then b) and self.coef[(row wire, mode index)] holds the residue series. The referee compares modes, weights, forms and coefficient residues with its own reference.
2. node_value(net, pk, labels, t, p, q, weights='paper', method='dp', basis='power'): pass basis on to NodeExpansion.
3. count_e2e(n, clauses, chunks=True, Lc=2, r=3, seed=0, a=1, u=1, basis='power'): the same construction as now with general a and u: labels with a coordinates from the same rng (as now), h = M * (2L - 1) // (sum over i < u of (L >> i) * (u - i)) + 1, qm = multiplicities(a, u, h), and NodeExpansion(..., weights='sharp', basis=basis) at every node. With a = 1, u = 1 the result must not change. Update its docstring.
4. appd_params.py: in choose_params, set newton=True together with the other code flags when USE_CODE_FLAGS (newton=False otherwise). Give rank_e a parameter cK=2.0, use it in both A.tup calls, and pass A.ck(flags) where choose_params calls rank_e (the frozen model uses cK = 1 when newton is on).
group_table, the three sums and byvars_value need no change: they only read self.modes and self.coef.
stop: smoke_appd.py prints SMOKE OK and then NEWTON OK

title: Shell matrix products with Strassen in the mode sum (shellmm flag)
spec:
Add appd-shellmm to appd_core.py: the group-by-group mode sum of sum_dp, done as shell matrix products with Strassen's algorithm. NOTES.md, section 'Round 7', has the math. Everything that exists must keep working exactly as now.

1. Module level, next to ps_add_mod: ps_sub_mod(a, b, m) returning [(x - y) % m for x, y in zip(a, b)]; naive_matmul(A, B, q, m), the schoolbook product (A is a list of n rows of k series, B a list of k rows of l series, a series is a list of q ints mod m, the result is n rows of l series); strassen_sq(X, Y, q, m) for S x S matrices with S a power of two: if S <= 2 return naive_matmul(X, Y, q, m); otherwise split X and Y into four h x h quadrants (h = S // 2) and return the four result quadrants from Strassen's seven products M1 = (A11 + A22)(B11 + B22), M2 = (A21 + A22) B11, M3 = A11 (B12 - B22), M4 = A22 (B21 - B11), M5 = (A11 + A12) B22, M6 = (A21 - A11)(B11 + B12), M7 = (A12 - A22)(B21 + B22), each computed by a recursive strassen_sq call: C11 = M1 + M4 - M5 + M7, C12 = M3 + M5, C21 = M2 + M4, C22 = M1 - M2 + M3 + M6 (entrywise ps_add_mod / ps_sub_mod). matmul(A, B, q, m) for an n x k and a k x l matrix: S = the largest power of two <= min(n, k, l); cut A and B into S x S blocks, using zero series [0] * q outside the matrices; result block (bi, bj) = sum over bk of strassen_sq(block (bi, bk) of A, block (bk, bj) of B); return the n x l result. Multiply two series only by calling the module-level ps_mul_mod (the referee counts those calls: at most 7^(k-1) * 8 for 2^k x 2^k inputs, k >= 1).
2. NodeExpansion.sum_mm(self): reset self.child_calls = 0 and build tables = {g: self.group_table(g) for g in self.r_groups} as sum_dp does. pos[g] = index of g in self.r_groups; for every mode k let lo, hi = min and max of pos[src], pos[tgt]. For the step of group g (index j): X = modes with lo < j <= hi that are not in self.inc[g]; Y = modes with lo < j <= hi that are in self.inc[g]; Z = modes with lo == j < hi. For each of X, Y and Z put the tuples self.tuples(idx, self.p) (as dicts) into shells by their exact weight self.weight(...), shells in increasing weight. Start with Phi = {(): [1] + [0] * (q - 1)}. In a step, for every X shell xl (weight w1) and Y shell yl (weight w2) with w1 + w2 < p: Am[i][s] = Phi.get(self.key({**x_i, **y_s}), zero series); then for every Z shell zl (weight w3) with w1 + w2 + w3 < p: Bm[s][j] = tables[g][self.key({**y_s, **z_j})], Cm = matmul(Am, Bm, self.q, self.m) (call the module-level name matmul), record (len(xl), len(yl), len(zl)), and add Cm[i][j] into new[self.key({**x_i, **z_j})] with ps_add_mod. After the step Phi = new; the step's shape list is the sorted list of its recorded triples. Return (Phi.get((), zero series), shapes, self.child_calls) where shapes is the list of the per-step shape lists in step order.
3. node_value(..., method="mm"): ser, shapes, calls = ne.sum_mm(); stats = {"shapes": shapes, "max_enum": the largest, over the steps, sum of n * k * l over that step's triples, "child_calls": calls, "modes": len(ne.modes)}. count_e2e gets a new last parameter method="dp"; with method="mm" every node uses ne.sum_mm() instead of ne.sum_dp().
4. appd_params.py: in choose_params add shellmm=False to the flags dict and shellmm=True to the USE_CODE_FLAGS update; give rank_e a last parameter shellmm=False, pass flags["shellmm"] to it from choose_params, and inside rank_e use A.eps_mode(r[d], {"modedp": True, "shellmm": shellmm}) instead of A.eps_dp(r[d]).
The referee checks matmul against a schoolbook product and counts its ring products; checks node values from method "mm", the shape lists, the shapes of every matmul call and max_enum against its own reference; and exact end-to-end counts with method="mm" and basis="ldu".
stop: smoke_appd.py prints SMOKE OK, then NEWTON OK, then LDU OK, then MM OK

title: Guarded Lagrange deformation (guarded flag, kappa per level)
spec:
Add the guarded Lagrange deformation (appd-guarded; NOTES.md, section 'Round 8', has the math) to appd_core.py and appd_params.py. GuardedPacking, guarded_multiplicities and guarded_h are already in appd_core.py (head code just above IMPLEMENTED; do not change them). Everything that exists must keep working exactly as now.

1. NodeExpansion.__init__: let guarded = getattr(pk, "guarded", False); for a guarded packing assert basis == "ldu" and weights == "sharp". (a) For a guarded packing build self.Wser only for pairs of real slots: for every packet P and every x, y in pkd["wire_at"], self.Wser[(P, x, y)] = taylor_at(pk.Wfrac(x, y), t, self.alpha, q); keep the old loop for ordinary packings. (b) In the LDU branch do not build Cpoly or G for a guarded packing (its pk.S is the node grid, not the set of differences). Instead, for the source forms use the coefficients [c * pk.colunit(xk[k]) for c in Um[m][k]] (and assert their integrality instead of Um's), and for the coefficient of mode m in row k use the row factor pk.rowfactor(xk[k], t, self.alpha, q) in place of G: cc = ser_mul(ser_mul(R_k, d[m], q), Lm[k][m], q). Everything else (the positions xk over the full virtual half, the weights a + 1 - i + 2b + 2 v2(b!), the weight asserts, the D.12 check) stays as it is.
2. direct_taylor_mod: for a guarded packing use taylor_at(pk.Wfrac(x, y), t, alpha, q) instead of the Wpoly / Cp0 series.
3. count_e2e: new last parameters guarded=False, kappa=2. With guarded=True the labels have u coordinates (tuple(rng.randrange(r) for _ in range(u))), pk = GuardedPacking(net, labels, a, u, kappa) and qm = guarded_multiplicities(pk, guarded_h(M, pk)); the rest (precision p + loss_bits(qm, a, t) per node, NodeExpansion with weights "sharp" and the given basis, sum_dp or sum_mm by method, recover(data, qm, a), the 2^unused factor) is unchanged.
4. appd_params.py: add module constants GUARD_KAPPA = 10 and _KAPPA = None. In choose_params add guarded=False to the flags and guarded=True to the USE_CODE_FLAGS update, then (after those lines, with 'global _KAPPA') set _KAPPA = GUARD_KAPPA if flags["guarded"] else None. Use the public assembly's helpers with kappa = _KAPPA wherever precision is computed: in min_a start from a = max(a, u + (_KAPPA or 0)) and loop while A.need_bits(lp_in, M, a, u, _KAPPA) > a - u + 1; replace every inherited-precision update (the A.lse2(math.log2(6 * ...) + a, lp, math.log2(4 * M * (a + 1))) expressions in rank_e, make and build) by A.next_lp(lp, M, a, u, _KAPPA) with that level's M, a and u; in rank_e multiply cK by A.gamma_guard(ad, _KAPPA) when _KAPPA is set (for both the arithmetic and the child term); in make add kappa=[_KAPPA] * levels to the returned params when _KAPPA is set.
The referee checks, with its own GuardedPacking objects on hidden cases, that NodeExpansion has exactly the reference modes, source forms and coefficients, that node_value (methods dp and mm) equals the direct evaluation, the by-variables leaves on chunk networks, and exact end-to-end counts with guarded=True; then it scores with the guarded flag (kappa from your params).
stop: smoke_appd.py prints SMOKE OK, then NEWTON OK, then LDU OK, then MM OK, then GUARDED OK

title: Better parameter search: balance-aware est_u, finer Lc and delta grid
spec:
Improve the parameter search in appd_params.py (NOTES.md, section 'Round 9'). Do not change appd_core.py; everything that exists must keep working exactly as now.
1. Set DELTAS = (1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3, 2e-3, 3e-3, 5e-3, 1e-2, 3e-2), LCS = (64, 256, 1024, 4096, 1 << 20) and TOPK = 20.
2. Rename the current est_u to est_u_pad (body unchanged). Add bal_u(rd, Md, delta, lam, d, a_prev, Lc): the largest integer u >= 2 that passes the frozen assembly's label-balance test at depth d. Copy the test from appd_assembly_public.exponent_of, section 'labels': lD = 2 u log2(rd), logM = lam + log2(Md), lnD = max(lD ln 2, 1); at d = 0 slack = log2(8192 Lc^2) + 2 log2(1/delta) + log2(ln(172 Lc) + lnD); at d >= 1 slack = log2(8) + a_prev + 1 + 2 log2(1/delta) + log2(lnD); the test passes if logM - lD >= slack (start from u = int(logM / (2 log2 rd)) and iterate u = int((logM - slack(u)) / (2 log2 rd)) a few times, then step down until the test passes). Define est_u(rd, Md, delta, lam, lp_in, d=0, a_prev=0, Lc=1 << 20) = min(est_u_pad(rd, Md, delta, lam, lp_in), bal_u(rd, Md, delta, lam, d, a_prev, Lc)).
3. Pass the depth d, the previous level's a (0 at the root) and Lc to every est_u call: in rank_e (keep a_prev = ad after each level), in build (the loop that sets the initial u, a_prev = ad after each level) and in full_ok inside build (a_prev = min_a(u0, 0.0, M[0]) after the root, then ad after each level).
check_t22.py runs choose_params(670, 'third') and checks that the frozen assembly gives a valid certificate with e < 1/3 (the current search needs 686). The referee re-scores every target with its frozen assembly.
